category: mathematical logic / proof theory; combinatorial group theory
literal_source_claim: The word problem for groups is undecidable.
canonical_claim: There exist a finite generator type and a finite set of relators such that no computable predicate decides whether an effectively encoded word represents the identity in the resulting presented group.
domain_and_universes: n : Nat; generators Fin n; rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n)); words : List (Fin n x Bool), where Bool selects a generator or its inverse; PresentedGroup uses the coerced finite relator set.
quantifiers: existentially choose a finite presentation (standard fixed-group reading)
universally range over finite lists of signed generators through ComputablePred
hypotheses: the generator alphabet and relator collection are finite/effectively presented
evalWord maps signed-generator lists into the free group before the presentation quotient
conclusion: The predicate deciding whether an encoded word represents the identity is not computable.
alternate_encodings: Two-word equality is equivalent to the frozen one-word identity predicate by multiplying one word by the inverse of the other; this transport is not yet credited.
excluded_degenerate_cases: Do not substitute undecidability uniformly over arbitrary presentations, undecidability of the semigroup word problem, or the assertion that every finitely presented group has undecidable word problem. Empty or trivial presentations cannot witness the existential conclusion.
